original_test_intent: Read the Redfish EventService root and confirm a readable, error-free service configuration response.
original_method: Follow the EventService link from the Redfish service root, perform one read-only GET over verified TLS and validate the complete service and delivery-policy document without following actions or altering subscriptions.
manual_activity: Supply the firmware-matched EventService schema, read-only credential handle, trusted CA bundle and policy for retaining event/subscription endpoint metadata.
safety_requirements: No embedded credentials or unapproved TLS bypass
Capture full JSON before projecting fields
Redact listener destinations, tokens and sensitive OEM configuration
Do not infer event delivery from ServiceEnabled
agent_execution_scope: Resolve EventService from the service root
Use secret-backed read-only access over verified TLS
Capture HTTP status and complete JSON
Validate ServiceEnabled, retry attempts/interval and supported event types when schema-defined
Inventory action and collection links without following them
Record no service or subscription mutation

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The GET matches the row, but the three-value projection contradicts the claimed full evidence and can hide retry interval, subscription capacity, status or OEM extensions; `-k` and exposed credentials are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover and GET EventService securely once, preserve the complete response hash, validate schema and delivery-policy fields, then produce a redacted summary without following subscription or event actions.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The EventService target and 15/10 timing remain; no expected enable state, retry count, event type or subscription capacity is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat EventService as a read-only capability and policy resource, retaining complete validated evidence while classifying all linked mutation paths as out of scope.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds service-root binding, verified transport, complete schema capture, retry/event field validation and sensitive destination redaction while preserving diagnostic logs.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Confirms advertised configuration only; it does not prove a subscription can be created, that an event reaches a listener or that retry behavior works in practice.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: ServiceEnabled may be true even with no usable destination or delivery path, and firmware-specific OEM fields may contain sensitive network data.

project_override_considerations: When retry fields are absent or nullable under the target schema, report their schema-defined state rather than invent defaults. Do not dereference subscription members during this root-only case unless needed solely to prove a link type and approved for redaction.
expected_evidence: No subscription/test-event mutation and preserved logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, Criteria and Script consistently target a GET of the EventService root. The source's weak security and generic criteria require improvement but do not conflict with the operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The missing access, schema and redaction inputs are standard read-only execution prerequisites and do not leave the test purpose indeterminate.

review_improvement: Preserves and validates the complete EventService policy resource rather than treating three projected fields as full evidence, while enforcing a strict boundary around event and subscription mutations.
independent_technical_reasoning: EventService describes delivery capability and policy, not proof of transport. Fields such as retry attempts, retry interval, supported event formats and subscription links must be interpreted together and against the target schema. A healthy or enabled root cannot demonstrate listener reachability or actual retry behavior. Complete capture is therefore needed for configuration audit, but mutation-capable links remain uncalled so this case stays low-risk and distinct from the following subscription lifecycle tests.
